headline: Watch: Iran tensions rose a notch (a reported strike on Iran's Sirik and Trump warnings) and a global Microsoft outage hit Australian services; nothing urgent for SA.
summary: Iran reports a strike on Sirik near Hormuz and Trump says he could strike again 'with no hesitation', while Tehran weighs leaving the nuclear treaty; a brief GPS-jamming flag over Israel this afternoon is not confirmed as a new attack. Hormuz traffic is still about 4 ships a day and Brent is about US$96, so SA fuel stays expensive. A global Microsoft 365 outage has disrupted Outlook and Teams for Australian hospitals and government agencies today; Microsoft says there is no sign of a cyber attack. Locally: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no bans or warnings, grid and phone networks normal.
actions: Keep the car tank and any generator fuel at least half full while Hormuz stays closed.
Do not rely on Outlook or Teams alone for anything urgent today; use phone or SMS.
Install this week's Windows, Outlook and Chrome security updates on family computers if not done yet.

categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict
categories.summary: Iran reports a strike on Sirik on its Hormuz coast and Trump warns he could strike again 'with no hesitation'; Tehran is weighing exit from the nuclear treaty and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi pipeline. GPS jamming over Israel spiked to 57% of a small sample of aircraft this afternoon, unconfirmed and now too few aircraft to measure. Taiwan pressure continues (Chinese 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific) with no live-fire warnings or jamming.

sources.title: Gulf News: Strike hits Iran's Sirik amid Trump warning to Tehran
Fox News: Trump 'no hesitation' strike warning as Tehran weighs nuclear treaty exit

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal and no private-jet movement to retreat destinations. Iran's talk of leaving the nuclear treaty raises long-run risk but there is no sign of any nuclear alert. The lit 'mobilisation' sign is a Russian recruitment story, not a call-up.

sources.title: Fox News: Tehran weighs nuclear treaty exit

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: A global Microsoft 365 outage has disrupted Outlook, Teams and other services across Australia, including hospitals, ASIO and SA Government; Microsoft says there is no indication of a cyber attack and recovery has been slower than expected. Phone carriers and the SA grid are normal, the global threat level is green and exploited-flaw counts are normal. The ACSC feed returned nothing this run.

sources.title: ABC: 'No indication' Outlook outage caused by cyber attack, Microsoft says
InDaily: SA Govt update as Microsoft outage disrupts ASIO
Michael West Media: Microsoft outage recovery 'not progressing as expected'

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria with no cases outside Africa. The lit 'chemical attack' and 'unexplained deaths' signs are false matches (a Syria trials article and a fitness story). Adelaide emergency departments are normal (only the Royal Adelaide is busy).

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges and no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or Bureau severe-weather warnings (the Spencer Gulf wind warning was cancelled). Four small fires active across SA; several outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz traffic is still only about 4 ships a day (versus 100+ before the war). Brent is about US$95.70 and the Australian dollar slipped to 68 US cents, so SA fuel prices stay high. Malacca, Lombok and Sunda routes into Australia are normal.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Brent US$95.70 (flat), VIX 18.7 (+6.9%), gold US$3,902 (+0.4%), AUD 0.680 (-0.7%). Markets calm overall; a weaker dollar and firm oil are the main cost pressures for SA households.

concerns.title: Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping
drivers: Iran reports a strike on Sirik on its Hormuz coast and Trump says he could strike again 'with no hesitation'; Tehran is weighing exit from the nuclear treaty and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi pipeline.
GPS jamming over Israel spiked this afternoon on a small sample of aircraft; no new Israeli or US campaign is confirmed.
Hormuz still carries about 4 ships a day; forecast markets cut the chance of a Hormuz deal by year end to about 25%.

scenarios.name: Standoff drags on, sporadic strikes continue
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices stay high and volatile; occasional regional servo shortages but no rationing.

scenarios.name: Deal reached, shipping recovers
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices ease over weeks; little direct effect on SA.

scenarios.name: Major escalation, renewed US/Israeli strike campaign or wider Gulf attacks
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel price jump and local shortages within 1-3 weeks; possible government fuel measures.

actions.action: Keep the car and any generator fuel at least half full.
actions.reason: In an escalation, stations run dry within days from panic buying; a half tank covers about a week of essential trips.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home.
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

concerns.title: Cyber attacks and outages hitting Australian services
drivers: A global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted email and Teams for Australian hospitals and agencies today; Microsoft says it was not a cyber attack. It shows how much depends on one provider.
Phone carriers are normal, the global threat level is green and Australian ransomware listings are below normal.

scenarios.name: Ongoing breaches and occasional cloud outages
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of disruption to email and online services; scam risk from stolen data.

scenarios.name: Hours-long outage of payments or a telco
scenarios.sa_impact: Card payments and phones down for hours.

scenarios.name: Multi-day multi-sector attack
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, fuel and communications disrupted for days.

actions.action: Keep devices and banking apps updated.
actions.reason: Most attacks on households exploit known flaws that updates already fix.

concerns.title: Local SA emergency (bushfire, heat, power) within 7 days
drivers: Fire danger is Moderate in the Hills with no fire bans, CFS warnings or Bureau severe-weather warnings; four small fires active across SA.
SA grid demand is normal with no reserve warnings; outback flood road closures are far from Adelaide.

scenarios.name: Quiet week
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Hot, windy day with fire bans
scenarios.sa_impact: Fire danger High to Extreme in the Hills; travel plans may need changing.

scenarios.name: Damaging fire or major power outage
scenarios.sa_impact: Evacuations, power and phone outages in affected areas.

actions.action: Check your bushfire plan and the CFS app alert zones before the first hot spell.
actions.reason: Early-season fires start fast, and decisions are easier made on a calm day.

concerns.title: AI-enabled attack (non-traditional)
drivers: Reports of an AI-powered attack on crypto firm Chainstack and hackers hijacking AI agents to steal cloud credentials; none targeting Australia.
A central bank warned of deepfake videos of its governor (overseas); the 'flash crash' sign is a false match and the Microsoft outage is not linked to any attack.

scenarios.name: Background AI-assisted crime and espionage
scenarios.sa_impact: More convincing scams and data breaches; no wide outage.

scenarios.name: Synthetic-media crisis (fake leader video or alert)
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of confusion, possible panic buying before it is debunked.

scenarios.name: Machine-speed attack on many systems at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, telcos, hospitals or the grid disrupted for hours to days.

actions.action: Agree a family code word for urgent calls.
actions.reason: AI can clone a voice from seconds of audio; a code word defeats fake 'I need help now' calls.

concerns.title: Taiwan Strait pressure
drivers: Chinese navy 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific and repeated combat patrols continue; this is pressure, not a blockade.
No live-fire warnings, GPS jamming or internet disruption around Taiwan; Taiwan Strait shipping is normal and forecast markets give about 2% for a clash before 2027.

scenarios.name: Routine grey-zone pressure
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Large announced drill
scenarios.sa_impact: Market jitters; no supply effect.

scenarios.name: Blockade or quarantine
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel, medicine and electronics disruption within weeks.

actions.action: Keep 2-3 months of any essential prescription medicines.
actions.reason: Most medicines are imported via Asian shipping lanes, which any blockade would disrupt first.

concerns.title: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak (Africa)
drivers: WHO reports the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria; no cases outside Africa.
No new unknown-illness cluster confirmed by WHO this week.

scenarios.name: Outbreak stays in Africa
scenarios.sa_impact: No direct effect; possible extra airport screening.

scenarios.name: Isolated imported case in a Western country
scenarios.sa_impact: Media concern; Australian hospitals manage under existing plans.

scenarios.name: Spread in Asia-Pacific
scenarios.sa_impact: Travel restrictions and health system alerts.

actions.action: Check Smartraveller before any travel to Central or East Africa.
actions.reason: Advice and entry rules can change quickly as the outbreak spreads.

concerns.title: Undersea cables and Australian networks
drivers: One Hong Kong-flagged vessel is on the routine watch list near Sydney's southern cable zone; all Australian carriers are normal.
No undersea cable damage reported near Australia.

scenarios.name: Routine shipping, no damage
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Single cable damaged
scenarios.sa_impact: Slower international internet for days; traffic reroutes via other cables.

scenarios.name: Several cables cut at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Major internet, payments and cloud disruption across Australia.

actions.reason: EFTPOS and card payments are the first thing to fail in a network outage.
